$note: Every PERMITTED foreground/background combination, declared explicitly. A pair not listed here is not an approved combination. Specs are dotted paths into design-system/dist/tokens.json; because semantic tokens are mode-paired, each pair is declared ONCE and evaluated in BOTH modes. Add `modes` to restrict. Add `debt: true` (or a mode array to scope it to one mode) to mark a known failure tracked in RECONCILIATION.md rather than fixed. As of v1 there are none.

$usage.body-text: 4.5:1 — normal body copy. NOTE: weight 600 does NOT qualify for the large-text exemption; only bold (700) does.
$usage.ui-boundary: 3.0:1 — WCAG 1.4.11 non-text: controls, focus rings, meaningful borders
$usage.decorative: exempt — measured and reported, never failed
$usage.print-body: 7.0:1 — body copy ON PAPER. Held to the AAA figure rather than AA, and not out of perfectionism: paper has no brightness control, no zoom and no theme fallback, and a clinical report gets photocopied, which crushes midtones. WCAG's 4.5 assumes an emissive display the reader can adjust.
$usage.print-large: 4.5:1 — print headings >=18.66px bold or >=24px regular. Declared by NO pair today, because every large element in the report already uses an ink that clears the stricter body bar. Kept so a future one has a class to land in instead of inventing a threshold.
$usage.print-rule: 3.0:1 — print non-text that MEANS something: data strokes, the chart's reference baseline, the pain dots.
$usage.print-decorative: exempt — measured and reported, never failed. Hairlines and washes the layout does not depend on.

$printNote: Print pairs do NOT declare `modes`. Their usage class selects the print token set, and contrast.mjs throws if a print pair declares modes or a screen pair asks for the print set — so a print colour can never be measured against the dark screen palette by accident.

DECORATIVE FILLS ONLY — chip backgrounds, icon tiles, chart bands. Exempt because a mark never carries meaning alone: a chip always has a label, an icon tile always has a glyph. Anything that CONVEYS meaning, including a chart line, must use the ink role instead.

THE BACKDROP CATEGORY INK ACTUALLY SITS ON. Chips, badges and trend pills fill with a 13% tint of their OWN mark, which lifts the backdrop toward the text and eats the margin. The ink was originally solved against plain white and reached only 4.44:1 here. Backdrops are the composited result (pastel.pain at 13% over white), because a background spec must be opaque. Light only: on dark, ink resolves to the pastel and clears 6.5-8.1:1 on the same tint.
Was 4.49:1 before recalibration.

THE WORST REAL BACKDROP, and the one the ink is now solved against. The fast-path check-in fills its SELECTED option with a 27% tint and renders the word in the category colour at 15px/700 — body text, because only >=18.66px BOLD qualifies as large. All five reached 4.08-4.36:1 before recalibration, and all five were undeclared.

TEXT ON A FULL-STRENGTH CATEGORY FILL. This combination existed in the product with no token and no declared pair: two buttons answered `#fff`, giving 1.81:1 and 1.58:1 in BOTH modes — worse than anything ever tracked as debt, on a button label in the free experience. The mark is mode-invariant, so one declaration covers both modes.

THE PAIN NUMERAL — 80px on the onboarding baseline screen, 22px/700 in the check-in sheet. Both are large text, so the floor is 3:1. Declared PER STEP because a ramp is a scale, not a colour: auditing one value says nothing about the other ten, and the failure it replaced was worst in the MIDDLE of the range (score 3, 1.37:1) where a spot-check would never have looked.
The value the captured baseline sits at. Was 1.56:1.
Already cleared before this work; the ink is the mark unchanged.

pairs.note: THE REACT NATIVE PORT renders combinations the web prototype never did, and none of them were declared until the port was measured. AnklePath screens put accent text directly on the page background, not only on cards.
Accent text inside an accent-tinted pill — the backdrop lavender.650 was re-solved against.
The 'Free plan unlocked' kicker sits on the page, not on a card.

SafetyAlert draws its warning icon and border on its OWN tint. Previously only measured against flat surfaces, so the one component that must never be unreadable was the one combination nobody had checked.
The trend badge word. Reached 4.39:1 before mood.ink was re-solved against this backdrop — found by measuring the port, not by review.
The report's pain figure sits on a card; the onboarding numeral sits on the page. Both backdrops now declared.

pairs.id: RN text/secondary as icon on muted fill
pairs.note: The Sign out glyph, and any neutral chip that puts a quiet foreground on the muted fill. 4.81 dark / 4.09 light against a 3:1 floor. Declared when Sign out was resolved to a NEUTRAL treatment rather than a destructive colour: this design system has no destructive role, and the only red it owns is reserved for red-flag guidance. NOTE the asymmetry that makes this pair ui-boundary and not body-text — text.secondary on this fill reaches only 4.09 on light, so it is fine for a glyph and NOT fine for a label. The trend badge learned that the hard way.
FIXED in v1 and mode-paired. Red-flag copy — the one thing a health app must not get wrong.
FIXED in v1. Was 4.38:1 dark and 3.78:1 light.
Icons, borders and fills, where 3:1 applies. Keeps the original hue.

RECLASSIFIED, not ignored. WCAG 1.4.11 applies to a visual indicator only where that presentation is ESSENTIAL to identifying the state. Selection here is carried by three simultaneous signals — a tinted fill, this border, and a trailing check glyph (verified on Figma node 1:222) — so the border is reinforcement, not the sole affordance, and the 3:1 threshold does not apply to it. If a future selected state ever drops the fill or the check, this must revert to ui-boundary and the tint must be strengthened.
The standard 13% tint background.

EXEMPT by specification, not by choice. WCAG 1.4.3 explicitly excludes text that is part of an INACTIVE user interface component from the contrast minimum. Deliberately still measured and reported so the value cannot drift unnoticed. Figma node 1:96 is the only reference for this state.

GRADIENT BACKDROPS NEED BOTH ENDPOINTS DECLARED. Only the flat-surface pairs were declared at first, so this card went unaudited — and its light mode was reusing the dark gradient's deep-indigo start behind near-black text at 1.58:1, the worst contrast in the system.
The binding constraint: secondary text at the gradient start is what set the palest usable light start value.
Sits UNDER the data line; the line carries the meaning.

10px italic, under the chart. The code painted a translucent accent here instead of this token — 3.58:1 dark and 2.99:1 light — and it went unmeasured because only `band` and `label` were ever declared, and `label` was declared as the TOKEN while the code used something else. Declaring a pair does not help if the screen does not consume it.

The two dashed boundaries. Decorative because the band fill and the 'common range for …' label each carry the range independently — but the dashes are what stop it reading as a single threshold, so this is the one corridor value where the CODE was right and the token was raised (20% -> 27%) to match it.

10px/600 — body text. Backdrop is phaseChip (accent @13%) composited over surface.raised, because a background spec must be opaque and the tint resolves differently per mode. The code put this label on an OPAQUE accent.dim fill instead: 3.84:1 in both modes, which is exactly what accent.dim's own token note forbids. Undeclared, so unmeasured.
This backdrop is why lavender.650 was re-solved: against plain white it cleared 4.85 and against this tint only 4.15.
The primary element on Progress — the chart supports it.
Gap-day copy. Inherits text.muted, which is now AA-safe in both modes.
Body copy, headings and the pain-dot numerals. Inherited from the light-mode ink.
Meta, labels, table cells, axis labels, footer. Replaces FOUR greys from the AnklePath template whose worst case was 2.36:1 as 11pt copy.
The binding case — ink.secondary was solved against THIS, the darkest thing it sits on, not against the sheet.
The wordmark and section emphasis. AnklePath's #1D6FB8 reached 5.23:1 here.
Declared because a trend word also appears inline, off its band.
The pain line and the masthead rule. Data, not text.
The chart's dashed reference baseline. It tells the reader where zero is, so it is meaningful non-text.
The dots sit on the pain stat card, not the sheet. Severity is read by COUNTING them — the fill carries no hue, so it survives a photocopy and does not paint a bad data point (N3).
Table rows and card edges. Exempt on the same argument as surface.border on screen: the layout separates these rows without the line, and a hairline forced to 3:1 would out-shout the data.
The unfilled remainder is the absence of a dot, not information.
Measured so the wash cannot creep darker: it must read as paper after a photocopy, not as a grey block.
Declared against the report's OWN surface token rather than relying on the text/primary pairs. report.heading is a ref today; if it is ever repointed, this is what notices.
Section rules and the range-chip outline. The layout separates without them.
The range chip and the back control.
The one failure this surface can legitimately report — the share sheet being unavailable. Export is free either way (N6).

THE dominant block. Backdrop is report.changeBlock (accent @13%) composited over report.surface, because a background spec must be opaque. Same composite as the corridor phase chip, and measured separately so a change to either token cannot pass on the other's evidence.

13px/700 direction word. INK, not mark — this carries the meaning and must be readable, which is the distinction InsightSentence got wrong at 1.40:1. Always paired with a glyph, so colour is reinforcement (N4).
Pain ink, NOT the safety hue. A direction of travel is a data point, not a red flag (N3).
The sparkline stroke. A sentence states the finding above it (P4), so the line is support, not the carrier.

Conditional content within ready, not a state, and the ONE surface allowed the reserved hue (N3). The callout was originally FILLED with safety.surface; on that tint it measured 4.24:1 in light and failed, so the fill was dropped for a border. A bordered callout is also the more restrained form §4.7 asks for, and the hue stays exactly where N3 puts it.
Guidance somebody has to ACT on. The hue signals; the words must be maximally readable, so they take the primary ink rather than the alert colour.
Load-bearing: with the fill gone this border is what sets the block apart from the report around it.

Steady gets no hue of its own — the absence of a signal should not look like one. It took text.secondary until that measured 4.49:1 on this tint in light. Under 4.5 by a hair, and a hair is still under.

The one piece of text guaranteed to be on screen before a user types — and it had NO declared colour at all until now. The field left it to the browser default, so it was unmeasured and unmeasurable. Declared against the capture family by name rather than leaning on text/muted on raised: these are refs today, and if either is repointed this is what notices.
The field outline on Home. Decorative on the same argument as surface.border: the field is a lighter surface than the page, so the surface step carries the separation and the line only reinforces it.
The resting fill behind the dictate glyph.
Load-bearing: this fill IS the save affordance appearing. Held to 1.4.11 rather than exempted.
The checkmark. Non-text, so 3:1 — and it is the glyph whose onClick was missing entirely until the field was extracted.
Same asymmetry the Sign-out glyph documents: fine for a glyph at 3:1, NOT fine for a label.

The FAB sheet's capture row fills with accent.surface; the backdrop is that composited over the sheet, because a background spec must be opaque. Same composite as the report change block and the corridor phase chip — measured separately so a change to any one of them cannot pass on another's evidence.

Primary ink at a smaller size, NOT secondary ink. text.secondary measures 4.49:1 on this tint in light — the FOURTH time this system has been caught by secondary-weight text on a tint of its own accent, after InsightSentence, corridor phaseLabel and the report change block. Recorded in §11 as a recurring root cause, not patched again in silence.

CLOSES A REAL GAP. The 13%-tint pairs above are declared modes:[light] only, with a NOTE asserting dark clears 6.5-8.1:1 — but a note is not a measurement, and the quick-capture tag chips render in both modes. An undeclared combination is unmeasured, not passing; that is the sentence this whole manifest exists for.

The tier headings on the Safety screen — the first place in the product where safety.* is the point rather than a passenger. On the PAGE, not on its own tint: safety.ink over the safety tint measures 4.00-4.24:1 and fails, which is the same trap the report's red-flag callout hit and the same resolution.

Guidance somebody has to ACT on. The hue is carried by the fill and the edge; the words take the primary ink so they stay maximally readable. Backdrop is safety.surface composited over surface.raised.
Load-bearing: with the words in neutral ink, this edge and the fill are what mark a row as a red flag rather than a note.
The uppercase kicker. Small and tracked, so held to body text rather than treated as decoration.
Saved state. Carries a star glyph AND the word, so the colour is reinforcement (N4).
The value shown BEFORE the gate (§9), on the page rather than in an accent card — see the unlock pill note for why the card was removed.

The pill was first nested inside an accent card, which tinted its backdrop TWICE and measured 4.28 dark / 3.95 light — a failure invented by the layout, not by the tokens. historyFade is contracted as a fade plus an INLINE pill on the surface, so the card was removed rather than the pattern bent. Backdrop is pillFill over surface.raised.

FIXED. This family carried the SAME defect as dayCard and nobody had found it: cardFrom referenced accent.dim (mode-invariant deep indigo) while title referenced text.primary (near-black in light), giving 1.58:1 — the identical figure §11 records as the worst contrast in the system. It survived because ShareCardScreen hardcodes #fff and never rendered the tokens. MilestoneDetail is the first real consumer, which is how it surfaced. Both gradient stops are declared, because a gradient needs BOTH endpoints as backdrops — the lesson dayCard already paid for.
Was text.secondary at 3.90:1 here — failing in DARK too, not just light, and declared in neither. Re-pointed at paper.400: 5.01 start, 7.59 end.

The Day-N label. It first used accumulation.counterLabel on a counterFill pill and measured 2.65:1 — because accumulation.* is mode-PAIRED while this card is mode-INVARIANT, so light mode put a dark lavender on a dark card. The card owns its palette: only share.* appears on it.
A footnote by contract — the milestone is the subject.
Doses that happened. accumulation.* by contract only ever accrues — there is no streak here and none can be built (N1).

A skipped dose. rest.* is contracted 'visually quieter than a logged day … never counted', so being faint is the POINT rather than a defect, and the row list states taken/not-taken in words directly beneath (N4). Exempt on the same argument as the corridor band.
The words 'Not taken'. Never 'missed', never red — N2 in one string.
The uppercase section kickers in the shared DetailScreen shell.
Answered questions keep a tick AND the word 'Answered' AND a strike — three channels, because a line through text is not one everybody can read (N4).
The paywall sheet rendered for the whole life of the prototype and NO pair had ever named it. Found by checks/consumption.mjs, not by review.
The grab affordance. Decorative because the sheet edge and the gesture both exist without it.
The dimming layer. Measured so it cannot drift toward opaque and start hiding that a screen is still there.

FIXED. savingsLabel referenced category mood MARK — a fill — and rendered it as TEXT: 1.58:1 on the sheet and 1.45:1 on this tint in light. Same mark-as-text mistake as InsightSentence, same 1.58 as dayCard and share.*. The SCREEN already drew mood.ink, so the defect lived entirely in a definition nothing rendered — which is precisely the class consumption.mjs was written to find.
A rest day's ground. Quieter than a logged day BY CONTRACT, so being faint is the design (N2).
The not-yet part of a counter. It only ever fills — nothing here can reset (N1).
The word beside a lock badge. Real text on a premium row — and premium rows are the one place this system is most tempted to let contrast slide.
Both gradient stops are declared. dayCard and share.* both shipped a defect because only one end of a gradient was ever considered.
The empty photo frame borrows rest.* — a photo not yet taken is the same kind of absence as a day not yet logged, and both should read as quiet rather than missing (N2).
The caption inside the frame. rest.surface is opaque, so this is its literal value rather than a composite — declared with the link anyway so the role reads as measured.

The outline on every accent-tinted container in the product — and it was named by no pair at all until the consumption chain was extended past the pattern layer. Decorative because the tinted fill carries the grouping without it.

The deep indigo gradient start on premium chips and rows. Its own token note warns it is NOT safe behind secondary text — which is exactly the mistake dayCard and share.* both made, so it is declared here as a FILL and nothing else.
Every bottom sheet dims through this. Measured so it cannot drift toward opaque and start hiding that a screen is still underneath.

The Toast, at the semantic level. pattern.toast.* refs these and was already declared; the underlying roles were not, so a change to either could have moved the pill without any pair naming what moved.

The sparkline's area fill, at 13% under the line. PainSparklineWithCorridor documents it as "a decorative wash under the line, carrying nothing" — the line and the sentence above it carry the meaning (P4). All eleven steps are declared rather than a sample, because measuring a representative few is how a ramp drifts in the middle.
